questions.prompt: What does Sysmon Event ID 6 log, and which earlier lesson depends on it directly?
options: DNS queries; the DNS Analysis lesson
questions.explanation: Event ID 6 (Driver Loaded) is the primary detection surface the BYOVD/LOLDrivers lesson relies on directly.

questions.prompt: Why can Windows Event ID 4688 alone be insufficient compared to Sysmon, even with command-line auditing enabled?
options: 4688 is deprecated in current Windows versions
4688 doesn't natively capture network connections, driver loads, or several other event types Sysmon provides
4688 requires a third-party license to enable
questions.explanation: Even with command-line auditing on, 4688 is limited to process creation — it doesn't cover network connections, driver loads, named pipes, or several other event types Sysmon adds.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson warn against deploying Sysmon with a default, unfiltered configuration?
options: The default configuration doesn't actually log anything
It generates an enormous volume of noise that can bury genuinely useful signal, making it not obviously better than no Sysmon at all
The default configuration is incompatible with most Windows versions
Unfiltered configurations require a paid license
questions.explanation: Excessive noise from an untuned configuration can bury real signal fast enough that logs never get reviewed — a tuned baseline (like SwiftOnSecurity's) is the practical starting point instead.

questions.prompt: Why does reviewing Sysmon logs only from local disk after an incident defeat much of their value?
options: Local Sysmon logs are automatically encrypted and unreadable
An attacker with sufficient access can tamper with or clear the local log the same way any other local artifact can be altered
Sysmon logs are only stored in memory, never on disk
Local logs expire after 24 hours automatically
questions.explanation: Local-only Sysmon logs are just as vulnerable to tampering or clearing as any other local artifact — central forwarding to a SIEM is what actually preserves their value for investigation.
